title: Orgrimmar
body: Orgrimmar is the capital of the Horde, carved into a canyon of red stone in the mountains of northern Durotar. Thrall raised it after the battle at Mount Hyjal, when he led his people to this harsh coast, and named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, the friend and mentor who had passed the Horde into his hands. Goblins, tauren and the Darkspear trolls helped to build it. The city is a maze of valleys joined by tunnels and ramps: the Valley of Strength behind the great gate, the Drag and the Cleft of Shadow, the Valley of Honor where warriors and hunters train, the troll quarter of the Valley of Spirits, and the Valley of Wisdom, where the Warchief holds court in Grommash Hold. Orcs and trolls share its streets with tauren and Forsaken. Not every enemy lies outside the walls. Demon cultists gather in Ragefire Chasm, the caverns beneath the city.

parts.body: In recent years the blood elves of Silvermoon, championed by the Forsaken, have joined the Horde. Their ambassador now speaks for Quel'Thalas in Grommash Hold, and beside her a blood elf master trains the paladins of his people in the power of the naaru.

title: Valley of Strength
body: Past the great gate of Orgrimmar lies the Valley of Strength. Here stand the bank, the auction house and the tower where wind riders come and go, and here too is the Broken Tusk, where Innkeeper Gryshka bids weary fighters lay their axes by the fire and tell of their battles, while a drunkard named Gamon holds up the bar. Overlord Runthak keeps order in the valley, and here, before the gathered city, he cries the Horde's great victories and mounts the head of a fallen foe for all to see.

parts.body: In the dark days after the Wrathgate the valley changed. Shops were shuttered by order of the Warchief, Gryshka and the other merchants grumbled about lost gold, and Forsaken refugees from the fallen Undercity crowded the approach, homeless and begging for help.

title: Valley of Wisdom
body: North of the Valley of Strength rises the Valley of Wisdom, the high seat of the city. Grommash Hold stands here, the Warchief's own fortress, and nearby the armor of Mannoroth the Destructor is displayed upon a great trunk. A plaque signed by Thrall names Mannoroth as the demon who first cursed the orcs with bloodlust, and bids the Horde remember how far it has come and how hard it fought to regain its honor. The wisdom of the spirits dwells here too. Shaman trainers of orc, troll and tauren blood teach in the valley, and the elder far seer Zor Lonetree, well schooled in the politics of the Alliance, sends young heroes wherever the land cries out for aid.

title: Grommash Hold
body: Grommash Hold is the fortress of the Warchief, built into the cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom and bearing the name of Grom Hellscream, whose blow slew Mannoroth and freed the orcs from the demon's curse. Guards still call it Thrall's Fortress. Its throne room is thick walled and windowless, and the Kor'kron, the Warchief's elite bodyguard, stand watch at every turn. Vol'jin of the Darkspear and the old warrior Eitrigg have long counseled Thrall at his side, and a guest named Mokvar, granted sanctuary by Thrall, takes care to bring his host no trouble.

parts.body: Since the blood elves joined the Horde, Ambassador Dawnsinger of Silvermoon has kept a place in the hold as well. She speaks softly for her people, the newest members of the Horde, and sends willing heroes out to its outposts to cement their bond with the rest of the Horde.

title: Cleft of Shadow
body: Off the Drag, a crevasse splits the rock of Orgrimmar, open only to a strip of sky, and in its gloom live the city's less savory folk. Warlocks of the Horde train here, insisting that the arcane corrupts only the weak, and the warlock Neeru Fireblade keeps a hut, proclaiming his loyalty to the Warchief. Rogues of the Shattered Hand teach stealth, deception and poison. At the bottom of the cleft opens Ragefire Chasm, the burning caverns beneath the city, where the cult of the Searing Blade hides under the felguard Taragaman the Hungerer and works in secret to lead innocent members of the Horde astray.

title: Valley of Honor
body: The Valley of Honor, in the northeast of the city, is Orgrimmar's martial quarter. Warriors drill in the Hall of the Brave, where officers of the Horde army muster and battlemasters send fighters to Alterac, Warsong Gulch and other fields of war. Hunters learn to hunt with pride, honor and tradition in their own hall, smiths and miners work the forges, and Ogunaro Wolfrunner keeps kennels of finely bred wolves, offered only to those the orcs count as true friends. Not everything here is war. An orphanage shelters children who lost their parents to the Horde's many conflicts, a quiet reminder of the price of all that glory.

parts.body: Of late the valley's old arena, where once only the stands could be reached, has opened its floor as the Ring of Valor. Arena organizers and a battlemaster gather challengers there, and fighters meet among platforms that rise and sink around them as they fight.

title: Valley of Spirits
body: The Valley of Spirits, a long and narrow valley in the southwest of the city, reached from the Valley of Strength, has long been the quarter of the Darkspear trolls. Their huts and lodges crowd its slopes, and in Darkbriar Lodge troll mages teach the arcane arts. The troll priests nearby greet strangers with a warning to respect their ways, or have a curse laid on them and theirs. Snakes of every color are for sale at Xan'tish's stall and staves at Ukra'nor's, and Warcaller Gorlach has the latest news from both continents and beyond for any hero willing to listen.

parts.body: Of late a portal shimmers on the upper floor of Darkbriar Lodge. It opens across the sea onto the Blasted Lands, close by the Dark Portal, and so speeds the Horde's travelers on the long road to Outland.

title: Thrall
body: Thrall, son of Durotan, is Warchief of the Horde. Born a Frostwolf and raised a gladiator slave in Durnholde Keep, he broke free, learned the ways of the shaman and freed the orcs from the internment camps, taking up the Doomhammer from the dying Orgrim. He led them across the sea to found Durotar. From Grommash Hold he preaches a new Horde: no demon spawned army, but a people of wisdom and honor who know when to show compassion even to a foe. He has worked hard to keep a fragile peace with the Alliance, knowing how much his people suffered in the wars of ages past.

parts.body: News from Outland shook even the Warchief. A messenger from Greatmother Geyah of Garadar told him that his father's blood lives on in that shattered world, and Thrall, his voice gone hollow as a storm cloud, learned that a grandmother he never knew still lives. He resolved to set his affairs in order and go to her.

parts.body: After the Wrathgate, Varimathras and Putress seized the Undercity, and Thrall swore that justice would be served. He sent his champions through portals from his own hold, followed them to the ruins and, with Sylvanas at his side, took the city back. Victory gave him little comfort. Gone, he says, are the days when Alliance and Horde fought side by side against a common foe, yet the march on Icecrown must go on.

title: Vol'jin
body: Vol'jin, son of Sen'jin, leads the Darkspear trolls. When Thrall's orcs freed his people from their captors on a storm swept isle, where his father was slain, Vol'jin pledged the tribe to the Horde, and the trolls followed the orcs to Kalimdor. Now he stands in the Warchief's chamber as an adviser, greeting each new champion as a sign that the fates smile on the Horde. He has no love for humans, and he has never hidden his doubts about the Warchief's dealings with them.

parts.body: When the sealed orders of Admiral Proudmoore's remnant reached Orgrimmar, showing that the admiral's plans against Durotar had outlived him, Vol'jin reminded all who would hear that he had urged Thrall countless times not to trust the humans. Then he set his pride aside and went at once to counsel the Warchief.
sources: quest 831 description and reward text

parts.body: When traitors seized the Undercity after the Wrathgate, Vol'jin went ahead of the Warchief to the ruins of Lordaeron. There he held the ground outside the fallen city, where Putress's apothecaries and Varimathras's demons had dug in behind their blight, and gathered the champions who came through the portals until Thrall and Sylvanas arrived.

title: Eitrigg
body: Eitrigg is an old warrior of the Blackrock clan, a veteran of the First and Second Wars. After the second he followed Rend Blackhand to Blackrock Spire, where both his sons were slain in the wars with the Dark Iron dwarves. Refusing to serve such a power hungry fool, he went to live as a hermit in the woods of Lordaeron near Hearthglen. Captured there by humans, he was saved from execution by Tirion Fordring and by Thrall, whose vision of a Horde free of demons won him back, and the Warchief made him an adviser in his throne room.

parts.body: He keeps his place in Grommash Hold still, a gruff and weary voice at the Warchief's side. When word of the Blackrock comes out of the east, it is Eitrigg that Thrall's people seek out first, for none knows the workings of the clan better than he.

parts.body: In time Tirion, now Highlord of the Argent Crusade, wrote to the Warchief asking for a good orc at his side, and Eitrigg went north. He serves the Crusade at the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak, studying the saronite the Scourge prizes and sending it on to Highlord Fordring. Yet he has not given up his place in Grommash Hold, and he is still found at the Warchief's side when he comes home.

title: Neeru Fireblade
body: Neeru Fireblade is the orc warlock of the Cleft of Shadow who claims he volunteered to aid the young Warchief, to prove that not every warlock of the Horde would rule it or destroy it from within. He counsels strangers not to trust too quickly, or distrust, for even friends serve their own ends. Shamans send him cult relics they cannot read, and he sends heroes down into Ragefire Chasm against the Searing Blade and its felguard master, sure that the beast's heart will please Thrall.

parts.body: His own counsel fits him best. Thrall knows Neeru for the true leader of the Burning Blade, yet leaves him in place rather than strike him down, meaning to use the warlock against the Horde's own enemies.

parts.body: To one he takes for a fellow cultist, Neeru speaks freely. Thrall, he sneers, is a fool who thinks his warlock works to cleanse the name of his kind, and the Burning Legion will drain this world and make ash of it.

title: Overlord Runthak
body: Overlord Runthak stands in the Valley of Strength, the orc who carries out the Warchief's commands without question and says of himself simply that he is Horde. It falls to him to proclaim the Horde's great victories to the people of Orgrimmar, gathering the city to celebrate its heroes and mounting the head of a fallen foe in the valley for all to see.

parts.body: The duty was not always his. High Overlord Saurfang once proclaimed the Horde's triumphs in Orgrimmar, but Saurfang has gone north to Warsong Hold in Northrend, and the task of crying victories to the city has fallen to Runthak.

The blow, he roared, would surely stir the Aspects from their malaise, and Deathwing himself reeled in pain and anguish that day. Then he mounted the head of the beast for all to see, and bade every passer by look upon the fallen dragon and know the might of the Horde.

title: Shenthul
body: Shenthul is a jungle troll of high rank in the Shattered Hand, the order of spies, assassins and poisoners whose rogues train in the Cleft of Shadow. The Hand names itself the veil over Kalimdor: its protectors, police, judges, jury and executioners. It counts the Deathstalkers of the Undercity as allies, and its spies have crept into the upper halls of Blackrock Spire. Even Thrall, its fence Jes'rimon claims, admits the Hand is needed. Its loyalty is less certain. Shenthul warns his recruits to stay vigilant against the changes Thrall would bring, since numbers alone will not overcome his rule, and his trainers speak openly of restoring the Horde's glory without the Warchief's timidity.

title: Hidden Enemies
body: Thrall will not tolerate traitors, but neither will he strike too soon and leave the rot to spread. So he turns to a young hero who can go where his agents cannot, to learn the truth and find the true head of the beast. The first task is to take a lieutenant's insignia from the Burning Blade at Skull Rock, east of the city. The insignia, Thrall says, will be a vital tool for infiltrating what he believes is the greatest threat to the Horde, and whoever carries it will soon stand in the midst of a war they never knew existed.

parts.body: With the insignia in hand, Thrall reveals his suspicion. A warlock within the city believes he has the Warchief's trust, but he is in truth the leader of the Burning Blade: Neeru Fireblade of the Cleft of Shadow. Thrall means to use him, not strike him down, and sends the newcomer to him with the insignia to see whether Neeru takes them for one of his own.
sources: quest 5727 description

parts.body: Neeru does, and speaks freely of the cult and of the Searing Blade leaders he values most, so Thrall marks them first. In Ragefire Chasm the satyr Bazzalan and the warlock Jergosh the Invoker are slain, and word soon reaches the Warchief that the caverns below Orgrimmar are in disarray and Neeru is more than agitated. It is a minor victory, Thrall admits, for the Shadow Council has more arms than can be cut away.
sources: npc_text 4533 to 4535 (Neeru's talk with the supposed cultist; Bazzalan and Jergosh)
quest 5728 description, completion and reward texts

parts.body: Sent back to stay close, the hero finds Neeru raging that Thrall's do-gooders have slain Bazzalan and Jergosh. Still trusting his new lieutenant, he lets slip that his agents in the Barrens and Ashenvale will begin the Shadow Council's newest scheme. Thrall had heard nothing of the Council in Ashenvale. His spies will look into it, and the Warchief will call on his hero again.

title: The False Warchief
body: Among documents taken from Blackrock Spire by the Kargath Expeditionary Force lies a claim that stuns Orgrimmar: Rend Blackhand, long thought dead, lives and calls himself Warchief. The news goes first to Eitrigg in Thrall's chamber, for none knows the Blackrock better. He tells how Rend and his brother Maim fled to the Spire after the Second War and fought the Dark Iron dwarves for it, driving them into the lower city only after Maim died and the dragons came, how his own sons fell in that war, and how Nefarian, brood of Deathwing, now rules the Spire with Rend as his servant. Thrall's answer is plain. Whoever goes must find a way through the Halls of Ascension, slay the false Warchief and lay his head before the throne.

parts.body: The head of Rend Blackhand is laid before the throne. With their Warchief slain, Thrall declares, the Blackrock are thrown once more into the maw of chaos. He calls on all Orgrimmar to honor the heroes who struck the blow and bathes the city in his blessing, so that the people of Kalimdor share in the victory.

title: What the Wind Carries
body: After Rend's fall, Thrall bids his champion sit and listen, for the wind carries news from the Eastern Kingdoms. The Shattered Hand has placed spies throughout the upper citadel of Blackrock Spire, and though their work is slow, they have learned things that cannot be ignored. The news concerns the black dragonflight, whose reach, it seems, extends well beyond the borders of the Burning Steppes. Thrall does not hide what he will ask of whoever hears it out: a task from which that hero may not return.

parts.body: Onyxia, brood mother of the black dragonflight, had disguised herself as a noble of Stormwind's court and bent Highlord Bolvar Fordragon to her will, until she was unmasked and fled to her lair in Dustwallow Marsh. Asked why not let the Alliance fall, Thrall only laughs. The Horde has peace, something its people have not known for ages, and he will not throw that away. But Onyxia cannot live so near the Horde's cities. He wants her destroyed.
sources: npc_text 5733 to 5738 (Thrall's account of Onyxia, the peace, the order to destroy her; the gossip completes 6566)

parts.body: One of Thrall's champions has found a way into her lair, and the hero is sent into Desolace to seek out the champion of the Horde who keeps the secret. Only the strongest of the black flight may enter, the champion explains, by many trials and a key enchanted by General Drakkisath himself, and one not of black dragonkin will find passage hard. He sets the hero on the road: an illusion woven by Myranda the Hag, then the trials of the old drake Emberstrife.
sources: quest 6567 description, base and mod-individual-progression rewrite (one of Thrall's champions found a way into the lair; seek him out in Desolace) and reward text (one way in; trials; key enchanted by Drakkisath; not of black dragonkin)

parts.body: The trials passed, the amulet needs only the blood of General Drakkisath in Blackrock Spire to awaken. Ceremony, the champion scoffs, is a pretty word for the bloodletting that amuses the black flight. With the general's blood the Drakefire Amulet comes alive, and the way into the lair of the brood mother lies open. It will be a victory, the champion promises, remembered for many years.

title: The Lord of Blackrock
body: Nefarian, son of Deathwing, ruled Blackrock Spire from its heights, lord of the upper city the Dark Iron dwarves lost once the dragons came. The false Warchief Rend Blackhand served under his command, and only those the black flight deemed worthy could pass the Halls of Ascension to reach him. Those who struck him down know the old feeling of victory. Before them lies the dragon lord's great head, scarred by countless battles, and a trophy like that has only one place to go: the throne of the Warchief in Orgrimmar.

parts.body: Thrall wishes only that he could have seen the beast's face as the killing blow fell. Yet he gives a warning with his thanks: the son of Deathwing lies dead, and surely the evil one stirs. He sends the slayer on to Overlord Runthak in the Valley of Strength.

parts.body: There, before the gathered city, Runthak cries out that Nefarian is slain, that the blow will surely rouse the Aspects from their malaise, and that Deathwing himself reels in pain and anguish this day. Then the head of the beast is mounted in the valley for all to see.

title: Alliance Relations
body: Craven Drok shares a truth about the orcs that is far from obvious. They are a proud people, and the war with the humans tried even Thrall's patience, but the Warchief is a diplomat at heart, and in his years among humans he learned much of their ways. Craven sends the curious to Keldran, a student of magic and other mystical arts whose hovel stands near the city's western exit. It begins with appearances, Keldran explains: how the Horde sees itself, how its allies see it and, most of all, how its enemies see it. As the Alliance pushes deeper into Kalimdor, it might wrongly decide that the Horde has made pacts with the Burning Legion, and Thrall cannot allow that. With his blessing Keldran has sent agents to Desolace to root out the demons there.

parts.body: In Desolace the fight against the Burning Blade and the satyr goes well, and Keldran's agents begin to hope they may go home before the seasons change. Keldran gives thanks for the work. Thrall desires peace between Horde and Alliance, he says, and a Horde seen to be clean of demons gives the Alliance no cause for needless war.

title: The Shattered Hand
body: Young rogues of the Horde who show promise are approached quietly. In Razor Hill, Kaplak passes word that Therzok of the Cleft of Shadow has an offer to make. The offer is a test. The Warchief, Therzok says, is too subtle and too cautious to unleash the might of the Horde, and the Shattered Hand means to win back the pride of the old conquerors, building strength in the shadows and striking where the enemy is exposed. First the recruit must kill Tazan, a troll who trades with the pirates near Ratchet, and bring back his satchel.

parts.body: Tazan is dead, but his satchel is locked and the key is not on the body. Therzok guesses that the troll left it in the care of his assistant Gamon, a drunkard most likely found at the tavern in Orgrimmar, and the recruit must quietly relieve him of it.
sources: quest 1963 reward text (locked satchel)
quest 1858 description (key left with Gamon, a drunkard at the tavern)

parts.body: With Gamon's key the satchel opens, and what lies inside impresses even Therzok. The recruit has more than proved their worth, and Therzok welcomes the newest member of the Shattered Hand with a gift he says will be a great help in the days to come.
